images.title: Three situations for a product
images.purpose: Sort products into three situations by whether each number is greater than 1 or between 0 and 1.
images.composition: Three equal columns side by side across the centre with wide gaps; a small colour key across the top; each column has one row of chips, one equation and one short result.
exact_structure: Colour key at the top centre: a teal #0072B2 rounded chip with the text greater than 1, and an amber #E69F00 rounded chip with the text between 0 and 1.
Column 1 (left): two teal #0072B2 chips side by side; below them the equation 3.4 × 6.5 = 22.1; below that a green #009E73 up arrow and the text greater than both.
Column 2 (middle): two amber #E69F00 chips side by side; below them the equation 0.75 × 0.4 = 0.3; below that a vermilion #D55E00 down arrow and the text less than both.

Column 3 (right): one amber #E69F00 chip and one teal #0072B2 chip side by side; below them the equation 0.75 × 5 = 3.75; below that a reddish purple #CC79A7 two headed horizontal arrow and the text in between.
Chips in the columns carry no text; there are exactly 6 chips in the columns (3 teal, 3 amber) plus 2 in the key.
Thin grey #6B7280 vertical divider lines separate the three columns.
rejection: chip colours not matching the numbers (3.4 and 6.5 teal, 0.75 and 0.4 amber, 0.75 amber with 5 teal)
the results attached to the wrong column
images.takeaway: Both greater than 1 gives a bigger product, both between 0 and 1 gives a smaller one, and one of each lands in between.
images.description: Three columns with coloured chips: two teal chips give 3.4 × 6.5 = 22.1, greater than both; two amber chips give 0.75 × 0.4 = 0.3, less than both; one of each gives 0.75 × 5 = 3.75, in between.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on the three situations.
images.teaching_notes: Have students read the chip colours first and predict the result line before reading the equation.

image_decisions.why: The three situations are a sorting rule, best seen as three side by side cases.
